text:
Echocardiographic ARD was studied in 260 consecutive intracranial aneurysm (IA) patients (Jan 2008–Dec 2010). ARD was larger in the "eccentric" group (age <55 with ruptured aneurysm, ≥7 mm aneurysm, or multiple aneurysms) than non-eccentric (P=0.049; multivariable P=0.02); similar in the <55-year subgroup (P=0.03), while hypertension favored non-eccentric (P=0.01). Height was inversely related to aneurysm size (P=0.004). Conclusion: some IA patients share an intrinsic wall defect with aortopathy, possibly from shared neural crest cell origin.

The phase 1/2 POSEIDON randomized trial (April 2, 2010–Sept 14, 2011; 13-month follow-up) compared allogeneic vs autologous bone marrow–derived MSCs in 30 ischemic cardiomyopathy patients with LV dysfunction. 20, 100, or 200 million cells were injected transendocardially into 10 LV sites. Primary outcome: 30-day treatment-emergent serious adverse events; efficacy included 6-minute walk, peak VO2, MLHFQ, NYHA class, LV volumes, EF, and infarct size.
